paper.title: llama.cpp b12503
paper.abstract: ggml-openvino: expand model support, optimize NPU,GPU and memory usage ( #32172 ) ggml-openvino: fix SWA mask detection When the SWA cache size matches the full cache size, identify SWA layers by the number of layers using each mask instead of cache size; the larger group is SWA, and a tie leaves the layers unclassified. ggml-openvino: fix SWA KV cache write indices Give SWA KV cache index tensors unique input names (a _swa suffix, like the masks) to prevent them from being merged with the full-attention cache indices. ggml-openvino: classify SWA layers only when the mask shows the window Two attention masks do not imply SWA: DeepSeek sparse attention uses two full-attention masks with the same name. When cache extents match, classify the larger mask group as SWA only once its mask has fewer keys per row than the other mask. Keep the classification per KV cache buffer so new sequences reuse the same graph, and include swa_layers when checking graph reuse. ggml-openvino: classify SWA layers from the first graph Waiting for the window to appear in the mask caused a mid-sequence graph recompile (~9 s for Gemma-4 at -c 1024 after position 512). SWA classification already gives each mask group its own mask, KV write indices, and attention size, which is correct whether or not the mask is a sliding window. Stateful mask rebuild recovers the window from the mask, or the causal mask for full attention. Classify the larger of two mask groups from the first graph and drop the per-KV-buffer bookkeeping. ggml-openvino: mark SWA fallback as a model-level heuristic Add a TODO above the equal-extent fallback to document that the larger mask group is currently assumed to be the SWA group. Since stateless graphs only require the two groups to remain distinct, this heuristic may only be necessary for stateful execution and could potentially be restricted to that path. ggml-openvino: derive attention sizes from the KQ mask shape Dynamic CPU/GPU graphs previously passed n_seq_active and attention_size(_swa) as separate inputs. Derive these values directly from the KQ mask shape using ShapeOf + Gather inside the model. This allows the GPU plugin to infer the Q reshape and KV slice shapes from shape inference rather than runtime input values. Q's head size also becomes static, enabling the fused SDPA kernel. GGML_OPENVINO_DISABLE_SHAPE_FROM_MASK=1 restores the previous separate-input behavior. The fused SDPA path also requires two supporting changes: Clamp the GPU mask to -30000. A key block that is entirely -inf for a row produces NaNs in the fused kernel. Restate the head count and head size after the KV slice. The plugin loses all slice dimensions when the end index is dynamic, causing SDPA to fall back to the reference kernel. Additional graph and quantization improvements: Skip the identity reshape of rows in SET_ROWS. Share a single Split for one-element view slices in dynamic GPU graphs (e.g. Gemma-4 per-layer embeddings), replacing one StridedSlice per layer. Add GGML_OPENVINO_REQUANT_EMBD=native (off by default) to preserve the file's native quantization for token_embd/output instead of requantizing to Q8_0_C. Include both environment settings in the graph and model cache keys and document them. ggml-openvino: only reuse Split outputs for exact chunk-aligned views The dynamic GPU path reused a Split output for any single-element view by deriving the chunk index from offset / stride. This produced incorrect results for views that were not chunk-aligned or whose remaining dimensions did not preserve the source strides, as seen in test-backend-ops CONT with use_view_slice. Restrict Split reuse to cases where the view exactly matches a split chunk, meaning the offset is aligned to the split stride and the remaining non-unit dimensions preserve the original source strides. Gemma-4 per-layer embedding slices continue to use the shared Split path. ggml-openvino: initialize ModelExtraInputInfo shape fields Initialize the newly added shape_source and shape_axis fields in the ModelExtraInputInfo brace initializer used by add_extra_inputs() . Without initializers for these fields, GCC emits -Wmissing-field-initializers , causing CI to fail with LLAMA_FATAL_WARNINGS . ggml-openvino: remove GGML_OPENVINO_REQUANT_EMBD The option identifies embedding and output weights by their tensor names, which are defined by core llama.cpp. Remove it from this PR; preserving the file quantization of these weights will be addressed in a separate change that identifies them by their roles in the graph. ggml-openvino: keep manual GQA attention 4-D The manual GQA attention path reshaped Q, K, and V to 5-D so that query heads sharing a KV head could broadcast against it. The GPU plugin cannot fuse this graph: it materializes the attention scores and copies the transposed K and V caches for every layer. Instead, stack the query heads for each KV head along the sequence axis (Q [B, H, S, D] -> [B, H_kv, factor * S, D]) and tile the mask accordingly. This keeps the graph 4-D from the MatMuls through the Softmax, allowing the GPU plugin to fuse the attention into its SDPA kernel and fold the K and V transposes into the fused operation. Clamp the mask to -30000, matching the SDPA path, because the fused kernel can return NaN when an entire block is masked with -inf. Models where the K or V head size differs from the Q head size now use the SDPA path, since the manual path assumes one head size. ggml-openvino: use a 4-D stateless KV cache on GPU In stateless GPU mode, bind the entire KV cache as a [1, ctx, n_heads_kv, head_size] tensor, with one token per row, instead of binding the first n_kv rows as a [1, 1, ctx, n_heads_kv * head_size] tensor. Write cache updates with ScatterUpdate along the token axis, and read the cache through VariadicSplit and Transpose . This allows the GPU plugin's StatelessKVFusion to replace cache reads and writes with in-place StatelessKV nodes, avoiding full-cache copies on every decode step and repeated memory pool allocations as the bound cache size grows. Set GGML_OPENVINO_DISABLE_KV_4D=1 to retain the previous layout. make embedding to have dynamic shape for OV GPU ggml-openvino: make the 4-D stateless KV cache opt-in add support for Q5_0 data type in OV GPU backend resolve CI test error ggml-openvino: fix -fa off and optimize grouped-query attention With -fa off, llama.cpp stores the V cache transposed, with value elements as rows and tokens along each row. The KV slicing code assumes one token per row and binds the wrong data when n_kv < kv_size. Detect transposed caches with GgmlOvDecoder::is_kvcache_token_rows() and skip slicing for them. For grouped-query attention, avoid repeating K and V for each query head. Stack the query heads for each KV head along the row dimension and let SOFT_MAX apply the scale, mask, and softmax so the GPU plugin can fuse the operation with the MatMuls. Read only the current layer's V-cache rows when layers use different cache sizes. Reject -fa off in stateful mode with a clear error and document that it requires stateless mode. ggml-openvino: fall back to stateless execution when -fa off With -fa off , the graph writes the V cache in transposed form, which is not supported by the stateful KV cache. Detect this pattern in compute_llm_params() as a SET_ROWS into a KV cache through a [1, n] reshape. When stateful execution is enabled, log a warning and fall back to stateless execution instead of failing graph conversion. Update the -fa off note in OPENVINO.md to document this behavior. Co-authored-by: Suhas Somashekar suhas.somashekar@intel.com ggml-openvino: preserve flat KV cache layout when -fa is off With -fa off, the 4-D KV cache layout introduced in #344 breaks MUL_MAT attention for Phi-3.5 mini and Phi-4 mini, causing oneDNN to fail with "could not construct a memory descriptor using strides". Preserve the [1, 1, ctx, n_heads_kv * head_size] layout when the graph writes a transposed V cache. ggml-openvino: extract Q5_0 weights when requantization is off Q5_0 weights are requantized to Q4_0, but test-backend-ops builds naive graphs, where requantization is skipped. Q5_0 then reached the normal weight extraction, which had no Q5_0 case, so every Q5_0 MUL_MAT and GET_ROWS op test failed with "Unsupported quantized type: q5_0". Extract Q5_0 as symmetric i8 weights (q - 16) with one f16 scale per 32 weights, the same layout as Q8_0. Models are unchanged: they still requantize Q5_0 to Q4_0. ggml-openvino: Optimize GDN output pre-scale for the NPU static path The NPU GatedDeltaNet kernel writes its output in FP16 and flushes values below 6.1e-5 to zero. Refine the code as review comments Add envs desc into doc Refine the code with removing duplicated env ggml-openvino: reuse graph bindings between decode calls Reduce host overhead outside infer() from 0.5–1.1 ms to 0.14–0.38 ms per token on Panther Lake. Reuse KV cache tensors and skip redundant port bindings. Use persistent USM host tensors for small GPU inputs and outputs. Defer graph-wide consumer lookup until after shape checks. Return model and compute params by const reference. Preserve tensor extras when memory, shape and type are unchanged. ggml-openvino: Add npuw dump envs for profiling Add the comments of new npu dump envs into doc ggml-openvino : ensure all leaves have unique names, remove input_srcs from graph key openvino: slice NPU prefill KV cache by active length Add GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_KV_SLICE as an opt-in NPU prefill optimization. When enabled, static prefill keeps the graph's attention dimension at the active prompt/KV length instead of expanding it to the full context capacity, and the KV-cache input/output tensors are bound with a shortened context axis over the same backing storage. This reduces the amount of KV cache and attention-mask data imported by the NPU plugin and lets the prefill graph plan smaller attention buffers for early prompt chunks. For example, with a 4096-token context and a 256-token prefill chunk, the first chunk can expose KV/mask dimensions at 256 instead of 4096, avoiding work over padded cache rows. The trade-off is graph stability: NPU static shapes now depend on the aligned active attention length for prefill, so a cached prefill model is reused only when the attention sizes match. Decode keeps a fixed full-context graph to avoid recompiling on every generated token, and SWA/ring-cache cases still fall back to full-size binding when the live prefix is not a simple leading slice. openvino: use L0 host tensors for NPU buffers Add GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_L0_HOST_TENSORS as an opt-in NPU buffer allocation mode. When enabled, non-remote OpenVINO backend buffers on NPU are allocated through the NPU default context with create_host_tensor(), and ggml tensor data points directly at that OpenVINO-owned Level Zero host allocation. The optimization targets the data path rather than the graph math: KV-cache and compute tensors can be passed back to the NPU plugin as OpenVINO tensors backed by importable Level Zero host memory. That avoids an extra ordinary-host-memory-to-plugin-staging copy on each infer boundary, which is especially useful for prefill where large KV/cache buffers dominate input and output traffic. If Level Zero host allocation fails, the backend logs a warning and falls back to the existing allocation path. The destructor tracks OpenVINO-owned storage so it does not free memory owned by the host tensor. The trade-off is that this is NPU-specific, consumes Level Zero host allocation resources, and improves transfer/import overhead without changing attention compute complexity or tensor shapes. openvino: fill NPU prefill masks directly Add GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_FAST_MASK as an opt-in NPU static prefill input-packing optimization. When enabled, the prefill attention mask is built directly in the OpenVINO input tensor instead of first materializing a padded std::vector and then copying that whole buffer into the tensor. The new fill_prefill_mask() helper writes each row once: it copies the valid mask prefix, fills padding columns with -inf, handles padded rows, and restores the causal diagonal to zero. This keeps the final mask numerically identical to the existing pad_input() plus set_zero_diagonal() path while removing one intermediate allocation and one chunk_size-by-context_size host copy per prefill chunk. The optimization targets CPU-side staging overhead, not attention math. It composes with GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_KV_SLICE: KV slice reduces the mask dimensions, while FAST_MASK reduces the work needed to construct whatever mask shape remains. The trade-off is a second mask construction path to maintain, with limited benefit for very small prompts or contexts. openvino: make NPU requant layout configurable Add GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_REQUANT_POLICY as the NPU-side selector for the default weight requantization layout. The existing NPU behavior remains the default: unset or group-128 maps quantized weights to Q4_0_128, while channel-wise selects the experimental Q4_0_C layout. Unknown policy values fail fast during model loading instead of silently compiling a graph with unintended weight packing. The optimization target is NPU weight bandwidth and compressed-weight code generation. Q4_0_128 keeps weights in a 4-bit symmetric layout with one scale per 128 values, reducing both payload bytes and scale metadata versus smaller groups while preserving a more conservative quantization granularity than channel-wise. Q4_0_C uses one scale over the innermost dimension, which can further shrink metadata and simplify dequant broadcast, but may cost accuracy because the quantization block is much larger. Include the selected NPU requant policy in the OpenVINO model cache discriminator. The same cgraph compiled with group-128 and channel-wise has different weight constants and dequant shapes, so reusing a cached decoder across policies would be incorrect. This keeps cache reuse stable within a policy while forcing recompilation when the layout policy changes. Trade-off: policy selection gives a performance/accuracy knob for NPU experiments, but all options still pay the load/compile-time requantization cost. The default remains group-128 for a safer balance of bandwidth, metadata, and accuracy; channel-wise is intentionally documented as experimental. openvino: centralize NPU plugin config overrides Add GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_CONFIG as the recommended catch-all override for OpenVINO NPU plugin and compiler properties. The value is parsed as comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs and applied after the built-in defaults and named NPU aliases, so advanced users can override any exposed property without adding a new llama.cpp environment variable for every plugin tuning knob. Keep the common knobs as named aliases for discoverability and compatibility: GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_COMPILER_TYPE maps to NPU_COMPILER_TYPE, GGML_OPENVINO_NPUW_FUNCALL_FOR_ALL maps to NPUW_FUNCALL_FOR_ALL, GGML_OPENVINO_NPUW_UNFOLD_IREQS maps to NPUW_UNFOLD_IREQS, and GGML_OPENVINO_COMPILATION_NUM_THREADS maps to COMPILATION_NUM_THREADS. GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_COMPILE_CONFIG is retained as a legacy alias for NPU_COMPILATION_MODE_PARAMS, while the documentation now recommends expressing it through GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_CONFIG. This keeps the public tuning surface compact while preserving high-signal aliases for settings with known performance or stability implications. NPU_COMPILER_TYPE can select the driver compiler, which currently generates faster prefill kernels on the tested NPU stack. NPUW_FUNCALL_FOR_ALL and NPUW_UNFOLD_IREQS expose NPUW graph lowering trade-offs around dispatch overhead, memory use, and long-context stability. COMPILATION_NUM_THREADS gives a way to cap compiler worker parallelism to reduce peak host memory during large graph compilation. Trade-off: a free-form KEY=VALUE string is less type-safe than one env var per option and invalid plugin properties will only be diagnosed by the OpenVINO stack. Applying it last is intentional: it gives one escape hatch for bisecting driver/compiler behavior and for testing new plugin options without rebuilding llama.cpp, while the named aliases continue to document the most important performance knobs. openvino: add scatter-elements KV update option Add GGML_OPENVINO_KV_SCATTER_ELEMENTS as an opt-in lowering for non-stateful single-row KV cache writes. When the flag is enabled and the set_rows indices are the simple decode case, translate_set_rows uses ScatterElementsUpdate with broadcasted rank-4 indices instead of ScatterUpdate. The motivation is NPU decode performance. The default ScatterUpdate path updates one KV row but the NPU plugin does not perform that update in place; it effectively copies the full destination tensor to write a small slice. As context length grows, that full-tensor movement dominates the per-token KV update cost. ScatterElementsUpdate expresses the same single-row write at element granularity and is measurably cheaper for this shape. Keep the optimization guarded. Stateful execution keeps its existing concat/update path, and multidimensional indices already use the broader ScatterElementsUpdate lowering. The new flag only changes the common non-stateful decode write, so the default behavior and graph shape remain unchanged unless the user opts in. Trade-off: ScatterElementsUpdate introduces extra ShapeOf, Reshape, and Broadcast nodes to build indices matching the update tensor. That overhead is worthwhile only when it avoids the NPU plugin's full-destination ScatterUpdate copy, so the path is controlled by an environment variable rather than becoming the unconditional lowering. openvino: gather token embeddings from compressed rows Add NPU token-embedding controls for models whose token_embd.weight would otherwise be widened from Q6_K to FP16. GGML_OPENVINO_TOKEN_EMBD_I8 keeps the embedding table on the normal int8 compressed-weight path, while GGML_OPENVINO_TOKEN_EMBD_I4 requantizes it to the group-128 int4 layout used by the NPU weight path. The performance target is tied embeddings and large vocabulary tables. When token_embd.weight is also consumed by the lm_head matmul, a normal Gather from the dequantized table gives the dequantization subgraph a second consumer and can force the full table to be materialized. The new gather_compressed_rows helper recognizes the dequantization chain emitted for int4/int8 constants, gathers only the selected packed rows from the leaf constants, and rebuilds the convert/subtract/multiply/reshape chain on those rows. This reduces memory pressure and avoids dequantizing or materializing a full embedding table when inference only needs the token rows for the current input. The helper is deliberately conservative: it only rewrites static 2D tables above a size threshold, walks only the known compressed-weight node patterns, limits recursion depth, and falls back to the original Gather when the subgraph is not recognized. Trade-off: int8 and especially int4 token embeddings can change accuracy and may not be faster for small untied embedding tables, because the rewrite adds extra Gather/Reshape nodes and only pays off when it avoids a large full-table dequantization. The default behavior is unchanged; the NPU-specific I8/I4 paths are opt-in through environment variables. openvino: stream u4 requantization chunks Extend the GGML_OPENVINO_REDUCE_COMPILE_MEM streaming requantization path to Q4_0/u4 targets. The previous streaming path intentionally skipped u4 because Q4_0 packs two weights per byte and the zero-point tensor stores two 4-bit values per byte, so the original quantize_q4_0 helper wrote as if every call started at block zero. Teach quantize_q4_0 to accept a destination block offset and use the absolute block index for weights, scales, and zero-point writes. Streaming requantization emits whole-row chunks in increasing order, and the target block size is required to divide the row width, so no target block straddles a chunk boundary. That keeps packed weight bytes aligned and preserves the even-block assignment before the odd-block zero-point OR for each shared zero-point byte. With that indexing in place, reduce-compile-memory mode can dequantize a chunk of rows into the scratch buffer and immediately quantize it into the final u4 buffers instead of materializing the entire tensor as temporary F32. This extends the peak-memory reduction already used by Q8/F16 targets to the NPU group-128/channel u4 layouts used for compressed weights. Trade-off: the u4 path is more sensitive to block alignment than Q8/F16 because of nibble packing, so streaming remains guarded by the same row-divisibility check and only runs when GGML_OPENVINO_REDUCE_COMPILE_MEM is enabled. When the flag is off, the full-materialization path and quantized output layout remain unchanged. openvino: fail fast on static recompile after weight release Extend the GGML_OPENVINO_RELEASE_WEIGHTS safety check to the static graph cache-miss path. Once host weight buffers have been released, any later compile would read invalid/zeroed host pages and bake the wrong constants into a new OpenVINO model. The dynamic path already rejected this situation. Static execution can still miss the decoder cache when graph shapes or model parameters change, so it needs the same guard before erasing cached infer requests and rebuilding prefill/decode models. This is a correctness and diagnosability change rather than a throughput optimization. It preserves the memory-saving release-weights mode for stable graph shapes, but turns unsupported recompilation into an explicit abort instead of silently producing a corrupted compiled model. openvino: add experimental NPU Q4_0 keep option Add GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_KEEP_Q4_0 as an opt-in escape hatch for NPU weight handling. When enabled for native Q4_0 tensors, the NPU requant path returns nullopt and keeps the original Q4_0 extraction instead of regrouping the tensor through the selected NPU requant policy. The motivation is to avoid unnecessary work for weights that are already stored as 4-bit values. The default NPU policy maps quantized weights to layouts such as Q4_0_128, which can reduce scale metadata but requires round-tripping Q4_0 through the requantization path. Keeping Q4_0 native can save that conversion work and preserve the original group-32 packing. Keep the option experimental and disabled by default. Current NPU driver/plugin stacks can compile the resulting group-32 graph, but inference may hang or fail with ZE_RESULT_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST. The default behavior therefore continues to use the safer NPU requant policy; this flag is mainly useful for debugging driver behavior, measuring the true cost of regrouping, and testing future NPU stacks. Trade-off: native Q4_0 avoids regrouping overhead and keeps the original quantization blocks, but it gives up the more regular group-128 layout expected by the default NPU compressed-weight path and may be unstable on current hardware/software combinations. openvino: unfold NPUW only for decode graph Compile the static prefill and decode models with separate OpenVINO config maps so the decode graph can opt into NPUW_UNFOLD_IREQS without forcing the same lowering on prefill. The build_static_model helper now receives the config map explicitly, and the decode path gets a copy of the base config with NPUW_UNFOLD_IREQS=YES when the user has not already set it. The performance target is NPU token generation. Decode executes a long stream of single-token infers, where folded NPUW function-call dispatch overhead becomes visible in every token. Unfolding the NPUW calls into separate infer requests removes that repeated dispatch cost and measured about +20% token-generation throughput on the tested stack, matching the behavior seen in OpenVINO GenAI. Prefill keeps the original folded config. Prompt processing is a batched workload dominated by larger matmuls, and the folded form is faster there while also using less memory. Splitting the config lets prefill and decode use the lowering that matches their workload shape instead of treating NPUW_UNFOLD_IREQS as a single global compromise. Trade-off: unfolding can increase memory and request-management overhead, so the automatic default is limited to the NPU decode model. If a user explicitly provides NPUW_UNFOLD_IREQS through the named env alias or GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_CONFIG, that value is respected because the decode override is only applied when the property is absent. openvino: tidy NPU tuning helper ordering Collect the remaining small cleanups from the NPU tuning series. This reorders the NPU KV-slice documentation and environment-variable cache entry next to the other NPU opt-in toggles, adds a short header comment for the centralized NPU helper declarations, and makes the static prefill attention-size assignment in the decoder a little more explicit. There is no intended behavior change in this commit. The purpose is to make the final source layout match the split commits that introduced the NPU tuning knobs, so future readers can find the related flags and helpers in one place without mixing that mechanical cleanup into the functional performance commits. openvino: normalize NPU compile env overrides Move the default NPU_COMPILER_TYPE=DRIVER setting into the NPU compile_config initializer so the default NPU plugin options are declared in one place. Route GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_COMPILE_CONFIG and GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_COMPILER_TYPE through the same set_compile_option_from_env helper used by the other named NPU compile option aliases. This keeps the legacy NPU_COMPILE_CONFIG mapping to NPU_COMPILATION_MODE_PARAMS intact while making all optional env-to-compile_config overrides follow the same non-empty-value rule. GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_CONFIG is still parsed last, so explicit comma-separated KEY=VALUE overrides continue to have the highest precedence over both defaults and named aliases. openvino: stream NPU weight requant by default to cut compile peak Default the streaming requantization path on for NPU so the compile-time F32 dequant transient (~1-2 GB for token_embd) is capped without an env flag. With the option set, the KV buffer is swapped for demand-zero memory at its first KV tensor and every KV tensor gets its own storage in a registry, grown in base*2^k rows (base = decode bucket or 1024) as the static graphs reach further. Host accessors, KV inputs and outputs, sliced KV views and the HFA past bind that storage; when it moves, idle requests bound to the old storage are recreated so it is released. With decode buckets and KV slicing the storage also takes the layout GenAI uses on NPU: K is [heads][rows][head_size] and V is [heads][head_size][rows], each bound whole to prefill and decode. SET_ROWS scatters new K rows on axis 2 and V rows on axis 3, the attention permute only cuts the window, the HFA past is the storage itself, and attention multiplies the probabilities by V^T with transpose_b instead of SDPA. A chunk-sized scatter on the innermost axis is slow on NPU, so the HFA prefill returns each chunk's V^T rows and the host copies them into the cache. Host reads, writes and fills go through a layout-aware copy, storage growth re-packs each head, and the layout is part of the model cache fingerprint. ggml-openvino: NPU weightless blob cache with one shared weights file GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_WEIGHTLESS_BANK=1 (with GGML_OPENVINO_COMPILED_MODEL_CACHE_DIR) exports weightless prefill/decode NPUW blobs plus one -.weights.bin. Weight Constants are laid out once by data pointer and their WeightlessCacheAttribute is retagged with the real offsets. Warm import uses ov::weights_path, and NPUW dedups both models into one bank through the LazyTensor hashes, so the OpenVINO weights_bank duplicate-uid patches are not needed. Decode KV-window models resolve the shared weights through the pair's file, or get their own file when the pair was imported. Also drop the old blob and manifest before publishing a re-export: std::rename does not replace an existing file on Windows. Based on anikulk/llama.cpp 4ab270a . Co-authored-by: Anisha Kulkarni anisha.dattatraya.kulkarni@intel.com ggml-openvino: prebuild all NPU decode KV windows with GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_DECODE_PREBUILD Decode windows were built lazily when the sequence first grew into them, which stalled generation for a compile without a cache and made a strict-mmap import fail for windows the export run never reached. GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_DECODE_PREBUILD replaces GGML_OPENVINO_NPU_DECODE_BUCKET: 0 (default) keeps decode over the whole context; 1 sizes decode by 1024*2^k KV windows and the call that builds or imports the prefill/decode pair also builds or imports the decode graphs of every other window up to the context, from the pair's graph and compute params. Requests are still created on first use. Window building is split out of the request lookup so both paths share it, and window ports are checked against the pair's decode ports. Revert "examples: add llama-chat-replay" This reverts commit 4eded2c . ggml-openvino: initialize the new compiled-graph and build-args fields ov_compiled_graph and static_build_args gained members, but three brace initializations still listed only the old ones. GCC reports -Wmissing-field-initializers there, and CI builds with warnings as errors. Set the fields by name, and pass {} for weights_path, which the window build sets afterwards. ggml-openvino: fix gemma-4 when only the output rows reach the KV-shared layers With one sequence, gemma-4 now drops the rows that are not output before its first KV-shared layer. Those layers take their positions through GET_ROWS(inp_pos, out_ids), and the backend mishandled three things: The positions are reshaped from [n] to [1, n]. That matched RESHAPE case 1, which marks the wrong dim dynamic. Use case 3, which keeps the source dim as dim 1. ROPE shared one sin/cos table per frequency setting, so the KV-shared layers reused the table built from the full inp_pos. Add the position input to the cache key. compute_llm_params took input_len from the last attention op. That is now a KV-shared layer with only the output rows, so the static (NPU) path padded prefill to the wrong length. Take the largest query length. Stateful execution still fails on the per-layer embedding view and is not covered here. ggml-openvino: keep the inp_pos layout for gemma-4's gathered positions A batch can have no output rows, for example a prompt chunk that llama-cli processes before its last tokens. gemma-4 then reshapes an empty position gather for the ROPEs of its KV-shared layers. The size checks of the RESHAPE cases cannot place a dim of size 0, so the positions got the wrong layout and the ROPE multiply failed on CPU and GPU. A RESHAPE that feeds the ROPE positions now always takes the inp_pos layout [1, 1, 1, n]. ggml-openvino: enable stateless GPU execution for MLA models The per-head MLA weights ( attn_k_b / attn_v_b ) are 3D quantized tensors. Their MUL_MAT operations were falling back to the CPU, splitting the graph at every layer and causing GPU execution to fail. Accept these tensors in the GPU support check and address the following issues exposed by enabling GPU execution: Quantization: Use exact zero points only for MoE expert weights. U4 weights with F16 zero points fail in batched GPU MatMul. Dynamic VIEW dimensions: Select the correct dimension when a size-1 dimension shares its stride (e.g. k_pe ), and match KV cache views by stride. KV cache V view: Translate the V view of the K cache as a reshape while preserving the dynamic cell axis. Flash Attention: Accept the MLA Q ( CONCAT ) pattern and V views derived from another view. Limitations: The GPU plugin fails on batched compressed weights with static shapes. Keep these unsupported in op tests and GGML_OPENVINO_FORCE_STATIC . openvino : use writable recurrent cache inputs Assisted-by: Codex ggml-openvino: fix decode crash for Qwen3.5 4B When the dynamic size is 1, the code now keeps the innermost match. When the size is greater than 1, it still uses the MLA rule, so the MLA k_pe fix still works for multi-token graphs. ggml-openvino: keep the GDN state in the OpenVINO layout Adds an opt-in switch, GGML_OPENVINO_GDN_NATIVE_STATE. When it's on, the GATED_DELTA_NET recurrent state stays in the layout the OpenVINO GatedDeltaNet op uses, [B, H_v, key_dim, value_dim], instead of the ggml layout [B, H_v, value_dim, key_dim]. That removes the two state transposes the translator adds on every call. ggml-openvino: support Ling-mini-2.0 group-routed MoE Ling-mini-2.0 selects experts by group, but the group-selection graph used ops that were not supported by the backend. This left 370 nodes on the CPU and reduced decode to ~1.5 tok/s. Translate the batched 4D GET_ROWS gather used for group scores. Support SET_ROWS for compute tensors, not just KV caches. Preserve the dynamic token dimension in FILL . Skip the DIV repeat when dimensions already match. Use the tracked token dimension for RESHAPE / GET_ROWS op cases, so a graph compiled during one-row warmup also works for ubatches with more output rows. ggml-openvino: disable output staging The backend stages small outputs (up to 4 MB) in a USM host buffer and binds larger outputs directly to the ggml buffer. When the number of outputs changes between calls to the same graph, as in llama-perplexity, an output port can switch from USM host memory to plain host memory. The OpenVINO GPU plugin mishandles this switch for some dynamic outputs, causing out-of-bounds writes on subsequent calls. This results in CL_OUT_OF_RESOURCES . For example, llama-perplexity -c 2048 -ub 512 fails on the fourth ubatch with Gemma-2, Gemma-4, Phi-3.5, Phi-4-mini, and Qwen3.5. Disable output staging until the plugin issue is fixed, so each output is always bound the same way. Input staging remains enabled. ggml-openvino: match attention masks by identity Gemma-4 prunes non-output rows before its KV-shared layers. These layers select the corresponding mask rows with GET_ROWS(mask, out_ids). Mask parameters were named by their consumers, but GET_ROWS is not recognized as a mask consumer. As a result, the sliding-window layers selected their rows from the full-attention mask instead of the sliding-window mask. This either caused the mask add to fail broadcasting beyond the sliding-window cache (d1024 and above with -ub 512) or allowed attention beyond the sliding window at shorter contexts. Track graph-input attention masks by identity and assign them the same parameter name for every consumer. The SWA pre-pass now keeps each layer's own attention mask, as the KV-shared layers read the same cache with mask rows derived from it. ggml-openvino: preserve input mask names and window sizes KV-shared layers appear at the end of the graph, and their derived masks are not graph inputs. Processing these masks overwrote the names and sliding-window sizes recorded from the original input masks with empty values. Preserve the names and window sizes of graph-input masks so the attention dimensions continue to be derived from the original mask shapes. ggml-openvino: accept empty tensors in stride checks In Gemma-4 batches without output rows, the attention tensors of KV-shared layers are empty. Their strides beyond the empty dimension are zero, causing has_strides_on_element_grid() to reject them. This sent SOFT_MAX, the KQV MUL_MAT, and CONT to the CPU with -fa off. It also caused the per-layer input crossing the graph split to be bound with the wrong layout. Accept empty tensors in the stride check. Their contents are never read, so the remaining strides do not need to satisfy the element grid constraints. ggml-openvino: classify transposed V caches using v_trans With -fa off, the V cache is transposed. When the attended length is the whole cache, as with a prompt that fits in one ubatch, its V view is contiguous and was mistaken for the K cache layout. The K layout path does not keep only the rows of the layer's own V size. Gemma-4 allocates 512 V rows in every layer, the size of its widest layer, and its sliding-window layers use the first 256. These layers then attended with all 512 rows, and prompts fitting in a single ubatch failed with a broadcast error. paper.title: External sandboxes for coding agents
paper.abstract: External sandboxes for coding agents I've been exploring new ways to sandbox code that is executed by agents, with a focus on making it safer to try out local models without worrying that a mistake or prompt injection attack might cause them to take damaging actions on a machine. I worked on this project with Prime Radiant , the AI research lab behind Superpowers and other projects . My post on the Prime Radiant blog introduces the external sandbox pattern, where code executed by the agent runs inside a dedicated sandbox while the agent itself lives outside of that sandbox. To demonstrate this pattern we've released three sandbox server implementations: external-sandbox-v86 runs a Node.js server which then uses v86 to run Alpine Linux inside WebAssembly. external-sandbox-container is a Python web server which runs the sandbox in Alpine Linux inside an Apple Containers instance. external-sandbox-quicksand is another Python web server, this time using Microsoft's Quicksand sandboxing library, which bundles QEMU and Alpine Linux in a Python package! Each of these implementations offers the same localhost API. You can then configure Pi, Claude Code, or Codex to send API calls to that sandbox any time they want to execute code. The sandboxes also include an optional HTTP/HTTPS allow-list proxy, so you can control exactly which hosts your agent's code is allowed to communicate with - plus a credential replacement mechanism to make authenticated API calls without sharing a secret with the agent. Here's the UI you can use to reconfigure that proxy while the sandbox is still running: I continue to be fascinated by the challenge of safely running untrusted code. This external sandbox pattern provides a neat way to experiment with different approaches. paper.title: GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol
paper.abstract: GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol OpenAI: We’re introducing GPT‑6.2 Astra, our new frontier model for your hardest projects, and GPT‑6.2 Sol, our efficient, versatile model for everyday work. They're available in the API as gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol . I shipped LLM 0.38 with support for the new models. 6.2 Astra is 80% of the price of 6 Astra - $8/MTok input and $40/MTok output, the same price as Claude Fable 5.2 (which was also 80% of its predecessor). 6 Astra and Fable 5 were both $10/$50. The cached price is an even bigger discount - $0.40/million compared to $1/million for the older model. This is great news for longer running agentic sessions. GPT-6.2 Sol is the same $2/$10 price as 6.1 Sol and 6 Sol - which are half the price of GPT-5.6 Sol ($4/$20). Here are the pelicans for GPT-6.2 Sol and for GPT-6.2 Astra . The 6.2 Astra max pelican looks like this: I have a full comparison grid here , but here's how the high/xhigh/max pelicans compare with the previous Sol and Astra releases: I also ran my most recent benchmark prompt against the two models, using "Ultra' effort levels in the Codex CLI: Make a three js animation where yonkers stands up as a big mech (cool stand up motion) and stomps around manhattan and queens and Brooklyn, use openstreetmap mapping data Here's Sol and here's Astra . Neither of them did a good enough job of morphing Yonkers into a big mech, at least in comparison to Claude Fable 5.2 and Gemini 4 Carbon . This video showing the Astra and Sol animations playing out at the same time: I created that video using GPT-6.2 Astra (Ultra) in the Codex desktop app by prompting: https://static.simonwillison.net/static/2026/yonkers-gpt-6.2-astra-ultra/index.html and https://static.simonwillison.net/static/2026/yonkers-gpt-6.2-sol-ultra/index.html are two videos of the same thing by two different models I need a video of the first 10 seconds where the top half of the video plays the first and the bottom half plays the second I need an overlaid label of "GPT-6.2 Astra" on the top half and "GPT-6.2 Sol" on the bottom half. These labels should be tastefully positioned. Make the video square and 2000x2000 pixels Then later: OK make it 20s Here's the exported transcript . The buzz around these new models is mixed at the moment. Astra 6.2 isn't scoring quite as high as Fable 5.2 on various benchmarks, and I've seen a few complaints that its communication style can be confusing. Theo Browne's review (in the form of a feedback letter he sent OpenAI during pre-release) has this useful example: When this model is working on long tasks, it can pull in a lot of subagents and manage them pretty well. It will then proceed to randomly ask you some weird internal implementation detail bullshit that you could not under any earthly circumstance understand, much less have input on . I sent "/goal make a new level for Outer Wilds". 2 hours in, it's "blocked" because it wanted to ask me "does r24's reviewer write it's clips to 24_g521.mp4 or 24_p11.mp4?"
